children: Meta Platforms (META, Financials), is giving its new Muse AI agent a physical home with Charm, a small handheld device designed to keep the assistant available without requiring users to pull out their phones.

Unveiled at Meta Connect on Wednesday, Charm is roughly the size of an Apple AirPods case. It has a 2-inch OLED touchscreen, speakers, microphones, front- and rear-facing cameras and built-in 5G connectivity.
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg described it as a way to bring the full Muse experience into a device that can sit on a keychain, in a pocket or on a wrist strap.

Charm is not meant to replace a smartphone. Instead, it acts as a dedicated interface for Muse and pairs with the Muse app on an iPhone or Android device. It can also play music and video, although it does not support phone or video calls.

The bigger idea is Muse itself. Meta launched the AI agent earlier this month with the ability to handle tasks such as sending emails, booking travel, filling out forms and making purchases for users.
Charm is expected to ship in December, putting Meta's latest hardware push on the market just ahead of the holiday season. Meta has not yet disclosed pricing.
The next catalyst is whether consumers actually want a dedicated device for an AI assistant and whether Charm can turn early interest in Muse into a broader hardware business for Meta.

title: Meta Just Made Its AI Ambitions a Lot More Personal
